$comment: Contract between backend and page. Source of truth: docs/designs/blob_design.md, section 'WebSocket protocol'. Every JSON message is an object with a string field 'type'. A message marked binary is followed, on the same socket, by exactly one WebSocket binary frame (the hub writes both under a lock, so nothing else comes between them).

utterance.binary: when dur_ms > 0: raw little-endian signed 16-bit mono PCM, 16000 Hz

fields.rate: int 16000 (send the number; the backend also accepts the string)

wake_clip.binary: raw little-endian signed 16-bit mono PCM, 16000 Hz (at most 10 s)

fields.label: pos | neg | auto: an enrollment sample of the wake phrase, of other speech, or an attempt the wake word heard (peak >= 0.1)
fields.peak: float 0..1, highest wake word score over the clip

fields.alerts: alert_item[] (active alerts only; empty before S4)

tts.binary: one complete WAV file (S1: the whole reply)

fields.timings: {stt_ms, hermes_ms, tts_ms, first_audio_ms, sc1_ms} (numbers or null)

GET /device-config?device=<name>.response: {device, sound, wake, quiet_hours, followup_listen_s, listen_no_speech_s, silence_rms, debug_audio}

POST /alerts.body: {key, source, text, urgency?, lang?, fire_at?|in_s?, ttl_s?}
POST /alerts.response: 201 new / 200 update {key, state, fire_at}; 422 invalid; 429 over 20 active

notes: alert_read: a failed synthesis or an unknown key answers error{bad_message}; a tap before the models load answers error{not_ready}
tts.followup is set for every device; the page must ignore it on devices with wake=false
wake_clip: the page sends it only when /device-config says debug_audio=true; the backend drops the clip when DEBUG_AUDIO_DIR is unset
